title: Haudenosaunee
capsule: The Haudenosaunee (Iroquois Confederacy) was a political league of five — later six — Iroquoian-speaking nations (Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga, Seneca, and after c.1722 Tuscarora) occupying the longhouse territory of present-day upstate New York, governed by the Great Law of Peace codified no later than the mid-fifteenth century. At its apex the Confederacy controlled the strategic Iroquois corridor between the Great Lakes and the Hudson valley, leveraging this position to dominate the fur trade and play Dutch, French, and English colonial powers against one another through the seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries. Devastating smallpox epidemics, the Beaver Wars of the 1640s–1700s, and ultimately the American Revolution split Confederacy unity: the 1779 Sullivan-Clinton Campaign destroyed most Haudenosaunee towns, and the 1782 Treaty of Paris left member nations divided between the United States and British Canada.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is moderately well attested through colonial-era maps, Jesuit Relations, and treaty documents, but pre-contact boundaries are conjectural; the dataset's 1450–1782 span reflects documented confederacy activity, not precise spatial precision.
